passage:
Noor: Can we stick to the cleaning rota? There have been dishes in the sink since Sunday and the kitchen is starting to smell.
Callum: You left a pot soaking for three days last month, so I'm not taking a lecture on dishes from you.
Noor: Fair, and I cleaned it. The pans in there now are still yours though.
cue: You left a pot soaking for three days last month
explanation: Callum answers Noor's complaint by pointing to her own past mess. Even if Noor slipped up once, the current pans are still unwashed and the rota still applies.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Callum isn't attacking Noor's character in general; he's saying she did the same thing, so she can't complain.

source: Teen to parent · car ride home
passage: Mom, you can't tell me to put my phone away at dinner. You answered work emails through Grandma's entire birthday party. So honestly, I don't think screens at the table are that big a deal. Can we stop for tacos?
cue: You answered work emails through Grandma's entire birthday party
explanation: The teen decides screens at dinner are fine because Mom also uses her phone at family events. Mom's habit doesn't change whether phones at the table are a problem.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: This isn't a random change of topic; it turns the criticism back onto Mom's own behavior to escape it.

title: Re: Q3 expense reports
passage: Hi Joanne, thanks for the reminder. Two receipts are missing because the hotel's billing system was down, and I've asked them for copies. On deadlines more generally, I'd gently point out that my June reimbursement sat in your approval queue for five weeks, so I'm not sure strict timelines are a fair ask of our team. Best, Tariq
cue: my June reimbursement sat in your approval queue for five weeks
explanation: Tariq gives a fair reason for two missing receipts, then deflects the deadline issue onto Joanne's slow approvals. Her delays don't make late reports from his team acceptable.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Tariq doesn't attack Joanne's character; he argues that her own lateness means she can't hold his team to deadlines.

passage: To the neighbor leaving one-star reviews about our patio heaters 'wasting energy': we've seen your SUV idling outside the school for twenty minutes every afternoon. Maybe start there. Our heaters stay on through March, and the spiced cider is back this week. Come in and warm up!
cue: we've seen your SUV idling outside the school for twenty minutes every afternoon
explanation: The café answers the energy complaint by pointing at the critic's idling SUV. That may be inconsistent of the neighbor, but it says nothing about whether the patio heaters waste energy.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: The SUV isn't just a new topic; it's aimed at the critic's own habits to deflect the complaint about the heaters.

passage: Councillor Mbeki has raised concerns that the library renovation is running 18% over budget, and I take budget discipline seriously. But I'd remind my colleague that the community pool she championed in 2022 came in 30% over, and no one on this side of the chamber demanded an inquiry then. I'd ask that the library receive the same good faith.
cue: the community pool she championed in 2022 came in 30% over
explanation: Councillor Vance answers a concern about the library overrun by citing Councillor Mbeki's own over-budget pool. Her past project doesn't explain or excuse the library's 18%.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: The pool isn't an unrelated detour; it's aimed squarely at the critic's own record to neutralize her concern.

title: Running app maker hits back at privacy watchdog
passage: Strydo, whose running app was found sharing users' location history with advertisers, responded Tuesday by noting that the watchdog behind the report, the Clearfield Privacy Project, 'tracks its own website visitors with third-party ad cookies' and questioned whether the group should 'lecture anyone on data.' Strydo said it would review its settings.
cue: tracks its own website visitors with third-party ad cookies
explanation: Strydo meets a report about its location sharing by pointing at the watchdog's own cookies. Even if the group is inconsistent, its findings about Strydo still need an answer.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Strydo isn't attacking the group's character broadly; it claims the critic does similar tracking and so can't criticize.

title: In-office Fridays and the leadership exemption
passage: The new policy asks all staff to be in the office on Fridays because in-person time improves collaboration. Leadership has exempted itself. If that reasoning holds, it applies most to the people we collaborate with most, and that's leadership. So either the rule should include them, or the collaboration case is weaker than the memo suggests.
cue: If that reasoning holds, it applies most to the people we collaborate with most
explanation: Rosa points to leadership's exemption to test the policy's own rationale. She isn't dodging a criticism; she shows the stated reason and the exemption can't both stand.

whyNot.fal_tu_quoque: Rosa isn't deflecting criticism of herself; she uses the inconsistency to examine whether the policy's justification really holds.

passage: My brother told me to quit vaping. He still smokes a pack a week, which is honestly kind of funny. But his point stands: I get winded on two flights of stairs now, my cough hangs around for weeks, and I'm spending about $90 a month on pods. Him not following his own advice doesn't make any of that less true. Day 3 without it.
cue: Him not following his own advice doesn't make any of that less true
explanation: Jonah notices his brother's inconsistency but judges the advice on its merits, citing his own breathing, cough and costs. That's the opposite of dismissing a point because the critic does it too.

whyNot.fal_tu_quoque: Jonah raises his brother's smoking and then sets it aside, accepting the criticism based on his own evidence.
